heading: Functions
title: Functions
description: Defining and using functions in Python

dataList.data: Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks. They help organize code, make it more readable, and allow for code reuse.

def greet(name):
    """This function greets the person passed in as a parameter"""
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")

# Calling the function
greet("Alice")
greet("Bob")
Functions can take parameters to receive input values.

def add_numbers(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add_numbers(5, 3)
print(result)  # Output: 8

def greet(name, greeting="Hello"):
    print(f"{greeting}, {name}!")

greet("Alice")  # Hello, Alice!
greet("Bob", "Hi")  # Hi, Bob!
Functions can return values using the return statement.

def square(x):
    return x * x

result = square(4)
print(result)  # 16
Variables defined inside a function are local to that function, while variables defined outside are global.

global_var = "I'm global"

def my_function():
    local_var = "I'm local"
    print(global_var)  # Accessible
    print(local_var)   # Accessible

my_function()
print(global_var)  # Accessible
# print(local_var)  # Would cause NameError
Functions are fundamental to Python programming. They allow you to break down complex problems into smaller, manageable pieces.
